text: After that night. <break time="0.8s" /> Adolph Myers came to Winesburg. <break time="0.8s" /> To live with his aunt. <break time="0.8s" /> An old woman who raised chickens. <break time="0.8s" /> And he stayed in her house until she died. <break time="0.8s" /> Although he was only forty. <break time="0.8s" /> He looked sixty five. <break time="0.8s" /> And he had taken the name Biddlebaum. <break time="0.8s" /> From a box of goods he had seen at a freight station. <break time="0.8s" /> He did not understand. <break time="0.8s" /> What had happened. <break time="0.8s" /> But he felt. <break time="0.8s" /> That his hands must be to blame. <break time="0.8s" /> And ever since then. <break time="0.8s" /> He had tried to hide them. <break time="0.8s" /> That evening. <break time="0.8s" /> Wing walked up and down his veranda. <break time="0.8s" /> Until the sun had set. <break time="0.8s" /> And the road beyond the field. <break time="0.8s" /> Was lost in grey shadows. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, still alone. <break time="0.8s" /> He went into his house. <break time="0.8s" /> Cut slices of bread. <break time="0.8s" /> And spread honey upon them. <break time="0.8s" /> For his simple supper. <break time="0.8s" /> When the rumble of the evening train. <break time="0.8s" /> That carried away the days harvest of berries. <break time="0.8s" /> Had passed. <break time="0.8s" /> The silence of the summer night returned. <break time="0.8s" /> And he washed his dishes. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, kneeling by the table. <break time="0.8s" /> In the lamplight. <break time="0.8s" /> He picked up the stray bread crumbs. <break time="0.8s" /> One by one. <break time="0.8s" /> And carried them to his mouth. <break time="0.8s" /> With amazing speed. <break time="0.8s" /> In that small circle of light under the table. <break time="0.8s" /> He looked like a priest at prayer. <break time="0.8s" /> And his quick, expressive fingers. <break time="0.8s" /> Moved like those of a believer. <break time="0.8s" /> Counting the beads of a rosary.
